title: Review: Sol third pass, fresh full review of the A5 integration PR
description:
READ-ONLY REVIEW. Do not edit, create, or delete any file; do not commit; do not push. Your only writes are bd notes on this bead and closing it.

SCOPE: the full diff of branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8 against origin/main (`git diff origin/main...HEAD`) — one PR carrying eight beads: eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.4 (character suffocation recovery gate, migration 0032, set_suffocation, calc breath formulas), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.5 (player-character death rules for encounter combatants, migration 0033), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.6 (adjust_hp knockOut), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.3 (adjust_exhaustion, derived level-4 HP maximum, level-6 death), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.11.4 (expend_ammunition / recover_ammunition, migration 0034), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.10.3 (roll_retained_check / resolve_retained_check / end_retained_check, set_surprised derived from comparisons, migration 0035), eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.6 (hydra Multiple Heads curated mechanic, tracked head count, derived reaction allowance, migration 0036), eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.5 (action:use-an-object ordinaryInteractionRuleRef -> rule:other-activity-on-your-turn, importer). Run `bd show` on each bead and on eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8 for the specs and acceptance criteria.

AUTHORITY: AGENTS.md; docs/design-and-pr-review-policy.md (profile rules-clause-complete); ADR 0020 §§2-3 (dice, arithmetic, atomic state mutation, resource accounting, state integrity are deterministic; adjudicated outcomes still pass through those boundaries); docs/design/rule-record-runtime-statements.md amendments A3-A5 and invariants 12-13; ADR 0015 (migration-first schema); docs/importer-fix-protocol.md for the importer parts; the committed SRD source text for every rule (packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json, records use the `key` field).

METHOD (review the mechanism, not the narrative):
1. For each capability, print the governing SRD source text beside the implementation and check source fidelity of every engine rule (thresholds, tie semantics, rounding, ordering, what counts as damage/healing, lifecycle start/end).
2. Check every model-facing surface (tool descriptions, schemas, Hybrid Contract in protocol.ts, known-limit statements in ruleKnownLimits.ts, error/rejection messages) against the real code: truthful, no model-side arithmetic/comparison or model-held canonical state offered as a fallback, target domain correct (character vs combatant), no stale wording from the pre-capability disclosures.
3. State integrity: atomicity (single transaction), invariants across the full state space (alive/dying/stable/dead, monster vs player-character rules, recovery block, exhaustion levels, closed vs active combat instances, missing/malformed rows), concentration and attunement side effects, campaign-actor sync, provenance conventions, deterministic ids/replay, write paths that bypass established helpers (mutateState, claimItem, removeItem), migration correctness (constraints, indexes, data preservation, contiguity, schema snapshot).
4. Write paths that let a model persist an unsupported/derived value (the A5 forbidden-substitution class), and any place a refusal could be bypassed through another tool (e.g. add_condition, update_combatant status, rest, level-up).
5. Test evidence: does each acceptance criterion have a test that distinguishes the bad state from the good state? Name missing evidence only where a real requirement is unprotected.
6. Sibling search: for each defect, look for the same class elsewhere in the diff.

REPORT with `bd update <this bead> --append-notes`, then `bd close <this bead>`. One entry per finding: ID (S1, S2, ...), severity (blocker / should-fix / nit), file:line, the violated requirement and its authority, a concrete failure scenario (inputs -> wrong state), and the minimal fix. Then a short list of what you checked and found correct. Apply the review policy's "From observation to finding" test: an observation without an operative requirement is "no requirement" in one line, not a finding. Do not stop at the first defect; batch everything you can find.

THIRD PASS — FRESH FULL REVIEW. Prior Sol reviews: eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.1 (S1-S15) and eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.4 (confirmation; S3, S4, S5, S8, S11, S14 open, S16-S18 new). Repairs landed through .8.2, .8.3, .8.5 and supervisor commits. Under docs/design-and-pr-review-policy.md, the combatant lifecycle classes have now been through two repair cycles, so this is a FRESH FULL REVIEW of the affected subsystem (encounter combatant lifecycle, campaign-actor lifecycle persistence/projection, HP lifecycle incl. exhaustion clamps, ammunition accounting) plus the whole PR — not a replay of earlier scenarios. First state CLOSED/OPEN for each of S1-S18 with fresh adversarial evidence; then report every new finding (IDs from S19). Apply "From observation to finding" strictly: speculative robustness is "no requirement". Close with an explicit overall disposition: APPROVE-READY (no blockers or should-fix findings) or CHANGES REQUESTED.
acceptance_criteria: S1-S18 closure plus any new findings recorded in bd notes with an overall disposition; no file changes; bead closed by the reviewer.
notes:
Fresh full rules-clause-complete review at HEAD e892bfc2ef921359d465e6250429b9fe3c34f2af, identical to integration branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8; origin/main 18c1b30575d082afcc6c2df76e981bcb7be7a9d1. Read all eight scope beads, the integration bead, prior review notes, batch-C decisions, AGENTS, review policy, ADRs 0015/0020, design A3-A5/invariants 12-13, and importer protocol. refs/beads/state is dated 2026-09-09 and lacks these rows; live bd records supplied current authority. Governing committed SRD texts were printed beside the implementations.

S12 OPEN in its remaining statement-boundary class: timing arithmetic is repaired, food/water/speed limits are retired, and hiding/surprise name actual wrong-tool traps. S17 CLOSED for reserved subtree injection/replacement: a fresh no-active-encounter model call injecting headCount 999 is refused specifically as engine-owned; unrelated state replacement on a suffocating, regrown actor preserves its head count, PC mode and block across reopening. Admission through other HP/status inputs is S3.

S3 | OPEN | blocker | packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:2091, :2115, :1261, :1318
Requirement/authority: SRD rule:death-saving-throws, rule:healing, rule:suffocating, condition:exhaustion and creature:hydra; .19.5.7.5 PC parity, .19.5.7.4 recovery prohibition, .19.5.7.3 level-six death; ADR 0020 §§2-3. Batch-C .8.5 S3 expressly requires participation never to suppress lifecycle derivation and exhaustion-six terminality on every write.
Fresh registry failures:
(1) PC-rules 20/20 -> hpDelta:-20 -> status:inactive (or escaped) in its own permitted call -> hpDelta:-20. The final call succeeds at 0 HP/status:inactive or escaped with zero failures instead of instant death. The life marker was overwritten, so the damage-at-zero branch no longer runs. Stable->participation likewise loses its stable marker/schedule; opting a monster's unconscious-at-zero knockout into PC rules leaves an unreachable unconscious PC state that neither death-save nor stabilization tools accept.
(2) PC-rules 1/1 -> adjust_exhaustion(delta:6) returns died:true but persists status:dying/exhaustion:6. The zero-result clamp overwrites the previously derived death. Sibling: an explicitly dead 1/1 PC combatant -> exhaustion +4 -> exhaustion -4 -> hpDelta:+1 becomes alive/1. Ordinary terminal-heal/status guards at maxima 5/24 work; this bypass is through the new clamp.
(3) Kill a recurring PC-rules actor, close combat, then start_encounter actors:[{actorId:'A',hpCurrent:10,status:'alive'}]. The actor and projection become alive/10 without revival. The same admitted inputs give a suffocating actor 10 HP while preserving recoveryBlock:suffocating, admit exhaustion-six actors as alive, and admit a zero-headed hydra as alive. This is a real registered alternate write path, not raw database corruption. The zero-head terminal input was established by a head-loss transition.
Minimal fix: keep canonical life state independent of participation, or refuse transitions that discard it; process mandatory death/damage outcomes despite participation status. Terminal death must take precedence over non-damage clamps and other statuses. Actor admission must preserve/validate existing lifecycle, refuse healing through admission while dead/blocked, and enforce exhaustion/no-head death; do not accept free HP/status as a substitute for qualified lifecycle operations. Normalize or explicitly refuse incompatible zero-HP opt-in.
Permanent evidence: generalized transition/admission invariant across death mode, life/participation states, base/effective maxima 0/1/larger, exhaustion/head terminal causes, separate-call sequences, and close/reopen with supplied HP/status. Proportionate because these are canonical death/revival and recovery-gate violations. Owner: combatant/actor/HP integration; material repair; required next state is invariant-preserving transitions plus fresh subsystem review.
S4 | OPEN | blocker | packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:356; real callers packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts:2903, :4787
Requirement/authority: ADR 0020 durable state/identity integrity; the existing F3 actor-persistence producer; .19.5.7.5 one-way PC opt-in, .19.5.7.4 persisted recovery block, .19.3.4.6 tracked head lifecycle; .8.5 S4 requires lifecycle continuity for durable actors.
Fresh failure through a real producer: instantiate a module goblin, link it to an until-removed summoning effect with campaignActorId:'durable', opt it into PC rules, drop it to 0, record a natural-1 death save (two failures), then suffocate it. Close combat and start_encounter with actorId:'durable'. The new projection is dead under monster rules, counters 0, block null: promotion copied HP/status/conditions but no combatLifecycle. A stable variant loses its recovery deadline and is projected dead. A module hydra variant loses a head with 25 damage, is promoted at closure, and reappears with source five heads and no pending regrowth instead of four tracked heads and one pending loss. Both effect creation and closure use ensureCampaignActorFromCombatant, which passes only existing state to upsertCampaignActor. The ordinary already-campaign_actor path now correctly synchronizes blocked regrowth and transfers pending facts; it does not cover this producer.
Minimal fix: transfer the actual source combatant's complete canonical lifecycle into the durable actor through the reserved engine seam when establishing/refreshing that identity, in the enclosing effect/closure transaction. Preserve unrelated state and correctly transfer/invalidate schedule ownership so the promoted actor's subsequent projection or recovery has one authoritative owner.
Permanent evidence: generalized real-producer promotion/close/reopen invariant over module/anonymous combatants with PC dying counters, suffocation, stable deadlines, and hydra lost/pending/fire-suppressed heads. Assert actor state and projected state together, rather than only already-persistent actor fixtures. Proportionate to irreversible canonical state loss across identity promotion. Owner: actor lifecycle integration; material repair; required next state is complete producer coverage and fresh subsystem review.
S12 | OPEN | should-fix | packages/core/src/rules/ruleKnownLimits.ts:152-161; packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolSetSuffocation.ts:27
Requirement/authority: design rule-record-runtime-statements.md R0, amendments A3/A4 and invariant 12: each known limit must name a specific Eshyra trap; tool-contract knowledge belongs in the participating tool descriptions, and source/countdown explanation alone is not a known limit. A5's intended bounded-limit classification does not waive those criteria.
Fresh full-surface check: lookup_rules/discovery will label rule:suffocating partial and expose a statement that only explains the source survival interval and maps drop/breathe and deathRules to tools. It identifies no remaining behavior of a named tool/state that contradicts or silently omits the clause. The recovery/death-rule capability gaps formerly supplying that trap have landed; ordinary relevant calls conform. toolSetSuffocation's own description is just 'Record the suffocation drop or breathing event for a character or combatant', while the invocation/timing recipe lives in the per-rule annotation. Food/water/speed retirement, hiding/surprise wrong-tool traps and CON formulas at -4/-2/0/2/6/9 are correct; this is the remaining positive-mapping class from S12, not renewed timing arithmetic.
Minimal fix: re-derive this row under R0. Retire it if no actual trap survives, or explicitly identify the source-backed participating-tool trap if one does; move the useful bounded drop/breathe timing and target contract to the tool's own description. Preserve the corrected survival-interval timing.
Permanent evidence: preserve the existing source-timing and runtime-statement separation assertions, adapting membership only to the justified R0 disposition and asserting the retained tool contract if the recipe moves. No broad new audit is warranted for this localized prose boundary. Owner: A5/runtime-statement integration; non-material repair; required next state is a conforming bounded statement or justified retirement.
S14 | OPEN | blocker | packages/core/src/state/hpLifecycle.ts:838-847, :876-879; packages/core/test/exhaustion.test.ts:502
Requirement/authority: .8.5 S14 expressly authorizes a due stable recovery at zero maximum to regain nothing, clear the deadline and leave the creature stable; ADR 0020 state integrity requires that authorized state remain valid for the canonical advance_time operation. The existing incomplete-schedule rejection must distinguish corruption from this newly valid lifecycle state.
Fresh registered sequence: initialize a character at 1/1; adjust_exhaustion(delta:4) -> dying at effective max 0; stabilize_character -> stable with a deadline; advance_time(minutes:240) succeeds, restores zero HP and clears all schedule fields as directed. The next advance_time(minutes:1) fails 'stable recovery schedule is incomplete for character(s): pc-1' and rolls back the campaign clock. Removing one exhaustion level does not clear the deadlock. A combatant sibling processes the first deadline identically and allows subsequent clock advances, demonstrating the target-domain inconsistency. The new test stops after checking the cleared deadline and never runs the next clock operation.
Minimal fix: represent/recognize the deliberately settled zero-regain stable state separately from a malformed missing schedule, while preserving rejection of genuinely incomplete/corrupt schedules and the accepted no-revival/deadline-clear rule. Do not restore a minimum-one maximum or invent automatic retry as a requirement.
Permanent evidence: generalized lifecycle-sequence regression across character/combatant, effective max 0/1/larger, first and subsequent advances, and deliberately settled versus actually incomplete schedules. Assert clock progress and persisted HP/life state together. Proportionate because one valid character state blocks all campaign time/rest progress. Owner: shared HP/clock lifecycle integration; material repair; required next state is valid repeated clock consumption of the authorized settled state.
S19 | should-fix | packages/core/src/state/ammunition.ts:237-255, :278; packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolRecoverAmmunition.ts:17; packages/core/src/rules/ruleKnownLimits.ts:250
Requirement/authority: SRD rule:weapon-properties says to recover half the expended ammunition; .19.5.11.4 selects floor(half) of the engine-recorded expenditure, with atomic custody/destruction; ADR 0020 resource accounting. Availability limits what can actually be returned, but does not change the number originally expended. The tool/known-limit wording is implementation prose, not authority to replace the denominator with surviving pieces.
Fresh reachable scenario: hold four identical arrows; expend_ammunition(quantity:2) twice in one battle. Destroy the first two-piece drop with remove_item(disposition:'destroyed'), an explicitly supported reserved-row operation advertised by claim_item's rejection. Close combat and recover at the same battlefield. The operation reports recovered:1/destroyed:1/movedAway:2, consuming one of the two surviving arrows; half of the four expended arrows is two, and two are still available. The algorithm first excludes the destroyed expenditure and sums present pieces, then halves that smaller quantity, discounting known unavailability a second time. Partial destruction of a drop is the same class. No permanent test exercises this supported composition.
Minimal fix: derive each selected ammunition identity's recovery entitlement from its immutable original expenditure quantities, then cap/apply that entitlement against actual available pieces without returning absent/destroyed pieces or double-counting rows. Retain enough expenditure identity to account for a row after deletion, and make the tool/known-limit descriptions match the source-grounded operation.
Permanent evidence: generalized accounting invariant varying original quantities, missing/partially destroyed physical pieces, and ammunition identities: returned count is bounded by both source entitlement and availability, while returned/destroyed/unavailable accounting balances. Proportionate to deterministic item-count loss on a permitted inventory operation. Owner: .19.5.11.4/integration; material resource-accounting repair; required next state is source-grounded expenditure accounting.
S20 | should-fix | packages/core/src/state/exhaustionMutation.ts:75-84; packages/core/src/state/actionEconomy.ts:1447-1458; packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolSetSurprised.ts:213
Requirement/authority: the existing exact campaign-rules binding/resolver contract (state/campaignRecordLookup.ts and ToolContext.resolveRulesPack), ADR 0020 positively selected provider-neutral operations, and .19.5.7.3/.19.5.10.3 capabilities. These model tools must operate on the same available bound stack as start_encounter/update_combatant; an installed add-on does not authorize silently dropping the resolver.
Fresh registry failures with the real installLateAmbiguityAddon fixture: the resolver is installed on ToolContext; roll_retained_check and a passive comparison against an ordinary goblin succeed. set_surprised with that comparison then fails tool_error saying the bound add-on is unavailable. It passes no resolveRulesPack into the state seam, and setSurprisedInTransaction explicitly uses undefined/default resolution for the head/reaction/legendary profile. Sibling: adjust_exhaustion(delta:1,combatantId) fails the same way because its updateCombatant call omits the resolver and updateCombatant now resolves creature mechanics unconditionally. An exact nonbundled base carrying otherwise unchanged SRD records reproduces both failures, while update_combatant with the same ToolContext succeeds. These are actual installed-stack consumer paths, not a proposed new mechanic.
Minimal fix: thread ctx.resolveRulesPack through both mutation inputs and every participating profile/head/mechanic lookup, using the already established campaign resolver boundary. Preserve exact-binding failures when a pack truly is unavailable and transactional rollback.
Permanent evidence: generalized tool-consumer parity regression using the existing installed add-on fixture, covering a surprised ordinary/hydra observer and combatant exhaustion with/without a resolver; assert correct mutation when the bound pack is available and no writes on genuine resolution failure. Proportionate to failure of the selected operations for otherwise supported bound campaigns. Owner: exhaustion/surprise integration; material consumer-wiring repair; required next state is consistent exact-stack resolution.
S21 | blocker | packages/core/src/state/hpLifecycle.ts:591-597
Requirement/authority: committed SRD rule:death-saving-throws, Damage at 0 Hit Points, makes DAMAGE equal to or greater than the HP maximum instant death; rule:temporary-hit-points distinguishes the damage event from buffered HP loss. ADR 0020 owns that threshold; .19.5.7.5 mirrors these rules, and this review expressly includes the full shared HP lifecycle subsystem. The initial-drop overflow rule remains a separate source clause (rule:instant-death).
Fresh registered source-boundary probe: character at 0 HP/max 20, dying (or stable), receives 10 temporary HP, then adjust_hp(amount:-20). It persists dying with one failure and instantDeath:false; critical:true gives two failures. It should die immediately because the damage at zero equals the maximum. Eight fresh cases (dying/stable x critical/noncritical x maxima 10/20) reproduce it. The branch compares overflow, after subtracting the temporary buffer, instead of the original damage. Its failure-count logic already correctly treats absorbed damage as a damage event; its instant-death logic does not. Combatants without a temporary buffer now correctly check full damage (S1), so shared-rule parity diverges. This is pre-existing in the character algorithm but lies within the expressly assigned fresh full subsystem review, and the PR changes the effective-maximum comparison here.
Minimal fix: at an already-zero-HP character's boundary compare actual applied damage with effectiveHpMax before failure accounting, while still consuming temporary HP correctly. Preserve remaining-damage/overflow semantics for the distinct initial drop from positive HP.
Permanent evidence: generalized source-backed threshold regression across dying/stable, critical/noncritical, below/equal/above effective maximum, and temporary buffers absent/partial/full. Assert instant death, buffer consumption and counter behavior; this preserves the exact source claim without multiplying near-identical reproducers. Proportionate to incorrect death outcomes. Owner: shared HP lifecycle integration; material repair; required next state is source-correct damage-event versus HP-loss accounting.
Checked and found correct, subject to S3/S4/S12/S14/S19-S21:
- Character suffocation preserves dying counters, blocks healing/stabilization/natural-20 HP regain and third-success stabilization, clears on breathing/death, and uses the normal concentration/attunement boundaries. Selected knockout consumes temporary HP, overrides lethal overflow, enters stable and arms recovery atomically.
- Ordinary exhaustion increments, reductions, caps, level-six death at nonzero effective maxima, long-rest final-maximum ordering, progression clamping and party/detail HP projections work. Non-damage clamps preserve temporary HP and hydra damage/head accounting; terminal precedence is S3.
- Current recurring-actor projection ownership follows active projection then combat-instance insertion order, not timestamps or ids. Old schedules transfer/invalidate correctly and archived manual mutations are refused. Reserved combatLifecycle state cannot be injected through start_encounter, and unrelated state edits preserve it.
- Ammunition reservations prevent ordinary claim/give bypasses and are excluded from nearby-item discovery. Even/odd and selected mixed-identity recovery, second-battle reuse, co-location/closed-battle checks, canonical custody/destruction and rollback evidence pass. S19 is the distinct original-expenditure versus remaining-availability boundary.
- Retained comparisons preserve the original check, strict observer-win ties, passive score adjustments, campaign/participant identity validation, ended-check refusal and fresh context visibility. Direct model surprise lists and supplied reaction totals are refused. The bounded resumption contract and real player-roll ledger, trace and audit-presentation consumers are wired.
- For the committed source hydra, the curated mechanic pins five heads, the 25-damage single-turn threshold, two regrown heads per lost head, fire suppression, ten HP per regrown head and zero-head death; reactions derive from tracked heads with opportunity-attack-only extra spends. Own-turn/skipped-turn settlement and blocked healing work on already-persistent projections.
- The use-an-object relationship resolves to rule:other-activity-on-your-turn, the actual combat free-interaction passage. Reviewed generated changes are limited to that pointer and source-pinned Multiple Heads curation. The exact-source importer guard, mechanics validator and evidence were inspected.
- Migrations 0032-0036 are contiguous. Constraints, indexes, row-preservation, adopted/migrated/fresh parity and generated snapshot tests pass. Unknown upgraded hydra head state is explicitly refused rather than reset or treated as one head.
- Retained gap-registry/audit infrastructure has its explicit retained disposition and a real nonempty injected report-projection regression.

Additional fresh S3 corroboration entirely through registered/source transitions: a 172-HP hydra takes five separate 25-fire-damage turns, reaches dead/47 HP/zero heads, then closes/reopens with actors:[{actorId:'A',hpCurrent:10,status:'alive'}] and becomes alive/10 HP/zero heads. No raw head edit is needed for that admission bypass.

No requirement: unlimited retained-check enumeration beyond the accepted most-recent-20 context bound.
No requirement: manual combatant lifecycle writes after encounter closure; the supervisor explicitly reserves that state to clock-driven recovery.
No requirement: automatically rearming the deliberately cleared zero-regain recovery deadline; .8.5 explicitly specifies clearing it. S14 concerns rejection of the authorized state by the next clock operation.
No requirement: generic configurable regrowth suppression outside the positively selected committed hydra mechanic.
No requirement: an additional permanent test merely because a throwaway review probe exists; published findings specify the operative invariant and proportionate replacement evidence.

FINAL DISPOSITION: CHANGES REQUESTED. Four prior findings remain OPEN (S3, S4, S12, S14); three new findings (S19-S21). Four blockers and three should-fix findings require disposition/repair before approval. Material lifecycle and accounting repairs require review of the repaired mechanism and its affected subsystem under the current policy. This bead may close because the assigned read-only review is complete.
